Will we have the internet in the future?

Probably, but the architecture and front-end of it may be very different from what we are used to today.

Many computer scientists anticipate the development of a 'semantic web' where information is tagged with 'metadata' as it's created. This will allow information to auto-associate in the way that our own memories work. Instead of using centralized search engines to continuously parse information and present us with search results, information will auto-associate and automatically link to what's related to whatever we happen to be doing. This would be conducted through what is called a 'semantic desktop' that would serve as an alternative to web browsers and perhaps computer operating systems. An advanced form of these semantic desktops would be 'social-semantic network' platforms which may become the alternative to today's social networking apps and social media. A social-semantic network would create a semantic web out of your personal information and anonymously auto-associate it with the webs created about other people and various services and systems useful to us. It would seek to arrange and mediate mutually beneficial exchanges. It would be like an Internet with a 'pronoia' imperative--a secret digital conspiracy trying to help you and everyone else.

Another possibility is that blockchain technology, now associated with Bitcoin, will evolve to become a backbone of the Internet. A platform for storing all on-line information in an indestructible encrypted form and eventually to become a kind of virtual distributed virtual computer where programs exist as independent, indestructible, self-running entities stored redundantly across the globe and driven by 'blind' data processing systems. Instead of having servers, routers/switches, and front-end personal computers the Internet would become a collection of generic devices performing all those hardware roles in one form/architecture, storing chunks of redundant encrypted data and doing blind processing, along with wirelessly-connected front-end displays that let us access our personal domains in this global blockchain space.

Many also believe that VR will have a much bigger role in the future Internet, evolving it into more of a place or space than a networked information repository. It might well become the native habitat of artificial intelligence.
